```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Burlot et al. (2026) report two final models for the intravenous Bcl2
inhibitor S65487, both fitted in Monolix 2023R1:

1. **PhI-II PK/PD model** (`Burlot_2026_S65487_pkpd`): a linear
   three-compartment PK model linked to an indirect-response model in which
   S65487 inhibits the formation (`kin`) of the Bcl2/Bim complex measured in
   PBMC, fitted to the phase I and phase I/II therapeutic-dose data (Table 2).
2. **Microdose-optimized (MO) PK model** (`Burlot_2026_S65487_microdose_pk`):
   the same three-compartment backbone with an added Michaelis-Menten
   elimination pathway and a Michaelis-Menten distribution into the second
   peripheral compartment (a Michaelis-Menten approximation of target-mediated
   drug disposition), fitted jointly to a 0.1 mg microdose in healthy
   volunteers and to the therapeutic doses (Table 3, Equations 1-2).

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Burlot_2026_S65487_pkpd"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.70288>

# Population

The analyses pooled three studies (Table 1): a phase 0 microdose study in five
healthy male volunteers (EXT 001; single 0.1 mg IV dose; median age 21 years,
median weight 83.7 kg), a phase I monotherapy study in 60 adults with
relapsed/refractory AML, non-Hodgkin lymphoma or multiple myeloma (study 002;
25-1200 mg; median age 67 years; 35% female) and a phase I/II study of S65487
plus azacitidine in 41 adults with previously untreated AML (study 003;
50-533 mg; median age 75 years; 41.4% female). Doses were given as IV
infusions on several weekly or intensified schedules (Supplementary Figure S1).

The PhI-II PK/PD model uses the 101 patients of studies 002 and 003 (1947
S65487 concentrations and 456 normalized Bcl2/Bim complex concentrations from 87
patients). The MO PK model uses all 106 subjects (2031 S65487 concentrations).

```{r population}
str(rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Burlot_2026_S65487_pkpd"))$population)
str(rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Burlot_2026_S65487_microdose_pk"))$population)
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment naming its source. Both tables
report IIV as Monolix CV% (`100 * sqrt(exp(omega^2) - 1)`), so each variance in
the model files is `omega^2 = log(1 + (CV/100)^2)`.

## PhI-II PK/PD model (Table 2, 'PhI-II PK/PD model' column)

| Parameter | Paper | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lcl` | Cl | 12.2 L/h | Table 2 |
| `lvc` | Vcentral | 7.6 L | Table 2 |
| `lq` / `lvp` | Q2 / V2 (1st peripheral) | 1.5 L/h / 16.4 L | Table 2 |
| `lq2` / `lvp2` | Q3 / V3 (2nd peripheral) | 15.5 L/h / 14.8 L | Table 2 |
| `lrbase` | R0 | 2.1e-4 ug/L | Table 2 |
| `lkout` | kout | 0.4 1/h | Table 2 |
| `limax` | Imax | 1 (fixed) | Results, 'Imax parameter was set to 1' |
| `lic50` | IC50 (study 002) | 140.9 ug/L | Table 2 |
| `e_study_s65487_003_ic50` | beta-IC50 STUDY003 | -1.6 | Table 2 |
| `etalcl`, `etalvc` | IIV Cl, Vcentral; correlation | 58.9%, 119.6%; 0.6 | Table 2 |
| `etalq`, `etalvp`, `etalq2`, `etalvp2` | IIV Q2, V2, Q3, V3 | 258.2%, 365.3%, 365.4%, 53.8% | Table 2 |
| `etalrbase`, `etalkout`, `etalic50` | IIV R0, kout, IC50 | 146.2%, 90.2%, 1386.5% | Table 2 |
| `addSd`, `propSd` | sigma Add, sigma Prop (PK, combined) | 2.9 ug/L, 0.5 | Table 2; Results 'combined model for PK data' |
| `propSd_bcl2_bim` | sigma Prop2 (PD, proportional) | 0.7 | Table 2 |
| `d/dt(bcl2_bim)` | `kin * (1 - Imax * Cc / (IC50 + Cc)) - kout * R` | n/a | Results; Supplementary Figure S2 |

## MO PK model (Table 3)

| Parameter | Paper | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lcl` | Cl | 10.5 L/h | Table 3 |
| `lvc` | Vcentral | 9.2 L | Table 3 |
| `lvmax` / `lkm` | VmaxElimination / KmElimination | 892.5 ug/h / 17.7 ug/L | Table 3; Equation 1 |
| `lq` / `lvp` | Q2 / V2 | 14.4 L/h / 19.6 L | Table 3 |
| `lk31` | k31 | 0.2 1/h | Table 3; Equation 2 |
| `lvmax_peripheral2` / `lkm_peripheral2` | VmaxDistribution / KmDistribution | 5105.4 ug/h / 145.1 ug/L | Table 3; Equations 1-2 |
| `etalcl`, `etalvc` | IIV Cl, Vcentral; correlation | 63.7%, 101.9%; 0.5 | Table 3 |
| `etalq`, `etalvp` | IIV Q2, V2 | 161.5%, 81.5% | Table 3 |
| `addSd`, `propSd` | sigma Add2, sigma Prop2 (therapeutic dose) | 6.7 ug/L, 0.5 | Table 3 |
| `addSd_microdose`, `propSd_microdose` | sigma Add (fixed), sigma Prop (microdose) | 0.001 ug/L, 0.1 | Table 3 |
| `d/dt(central)`, `d/dt(peripheral2)` | Equations 1-2 | n/a | Results; Supplementary Figure S7 |

```{r models}
mod_pkpd <- readModelDb("Burlot_2026_S65487_pkpd")
mod_mo <- readModelDb("Burlot_2026_S65487_microdose_pk")
```

# PhI-II PK/PD model: Bcl2/Bim complex inhibition

## Figure 2: typical-value profiles

Figure 2 of the paper shows the normalized Bcl2/Bim complex change from
baseline at 50-1200 mg on two schedules (A: days 1, 3, 5 and 8; B: days 1-5,
8 and 9), separately for the phase I (study 002) and phase I/II (study 003)
IC50. Infusions are simulated over 0.5 h (see Assumptions).

```{r fig2-events}
doses_fig2 <- c(50, 100, 150, 300, 500, 800, 1000, 1200)
schedules <- list(
  "A: days 1, 3, 5, 8" = c(1, 3, 5, 8),
  "B: days 1-5, 8, 9" = c(1:5, 8, 9)
)
obs_times <- seq(0, 240, by = 0.5)

make_arm <- function(id, dose, days, study, schedule, n = 1L) {
  ids <- id - 1L + seq_len(n)
  dosing <- tidyr::crossing(id = ids, time = (days - 1) * 24) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 1L, amt = dose, dur = 0.5, cmt = "central")
  # Two declared endpoints (Cc and the bcl2_bim state): observation rows name
  # the state endpoint; rxode2 still returns Cc on every row.
  obs <- tidyr::crossing(id = ids, time = obs_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 0L, amt = NA_real_, dur = NA_real_, cmt = "bcl2_bim")
  dplyr::bind_rows(dosing, obs) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      STUDY_S65487_003 = study,
      dose = dose,
      schedule = schedule
    ) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

arms_fig2 <- tidyr::crossing(
  dose = doses_fig2,
  schedule = names(schedules),
  study = c(0L, 1L)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = seq_len(dplyr::n()))

ev_fig2 <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms_fig2)), function(i) {
  a <- arms_fig2[i, ]
  make_arm(a$id, a$dose, schedules[[a$schedule]], a$study, a$schedule)
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(ev_fig2[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

```{r fig2, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6}
sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_pkpd,
  events = ev_fig2,
  omega = NA,
  sigma = NA,
  useLinCmt = FALSE,
  keep = c("dose", "schedule", "STUDY_S65487_003")
) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::group_by(id) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct = 100 * (bcl2_bim / bcl2_bim[1] - 1)) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    study = ifelse(STUDY_S65487_003 == 1, "Phase I/II (003)", "Phase I (002)"),
    dose_f = factor(paste(dose, "mg"), levels = paste(doses_fig2, "mg"))
  )

ggplot(sim_typ, aes(time, pct, colour = dose_f)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(schedule ~ study) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 240, by = 24)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)",
    y = "Bcl2/Bim complex change from baseline (%)",
    colour = "Dose",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 2 of Burlot 2026 (typical-value prediction)."
  )
```

## Maximum predicted reduction

The Results report the maximum predicted reduction of the complex at the top
dose: 85.8% (schedule A) and 91.4% (schedule B) for the phase I population, and
94.7% and 97.6% for the phase I/II population, from simulations of 2000 virtual
patients per scenario. The figure axis is the change from the baseline
*median*, so the published numbers are population medians, not typical-value
predictions; with an IC50 IIV of 1386% CV the two differ by several percentage
points. The check below therefore simulates 200 patients per scenario with
between-subject variability and takes the median change from baseline at each
time.

```{r maxred}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20260617)
n_arm <- 200L
arms_max <- tidyr::crossing(schedule = names(schedules), study = c(0L, 1L)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id0 = (seq_len(dplyr::n()) - 1L) * n_arm + 1L)
ev_max <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms_max)), function(i) {
  a <- arms_max[i, ]
  make_arm(a$id0, 1200, schedules[[a$schedule]], a$study, a$schedule, n = n_arm)
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(ev_max[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))

sim_max <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_pkpd,
  events = ev_max,
  useLinCmt = FALSE,
  keep = c("schedule", "STUDY_S65487_003")
) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, bcl2_bim, schedule, STUDY_S65487_003) |>
  dplyr::group_by(id) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct = 100 * (bcl2_bim / bcl2_bim[1] - 1)) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()

max_red <- sim_max |>
  dplyr::group_by(schedule, STUDY_S65487_003, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(med = median(pct), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::group_by(schedule, STUDY_S65487_003) |>
  dplyr::summarise(simulated = -min(med), .groups = "drop")

typ_red <- sim_typ |>
  dplyr::filter(dose == 1200) |>
  dplyr::group_by(schedule, STUDY_S65487_003) |>
  dplyr::summarise(typical = -min(pct), .groups = "drop")

published_red <- tibble::tribble(
  ~schedule, ~STUDY_S65487_003, ~published,
  "A: days 1, 3, 5, 8", 0L, 85.8,
  "B: days 1-5, 8, 9", 0L, 91.4,
  "A: days 1, 3, 5, 8", 1L, 94.7,
  "B: days 1-5, 8, 9", 1L, 97.6
)

tab_red <- published_red |>
  dplyr::left_join(max_red, by = c("schedule", "STUDY_S65487_003")) |>
  dplyr::left_join(typ_red, by = c("schedule", "STUDY_S65487_003")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    population = ifelse(STUDY_S65487_003 == 1, "Phase I/II (003)", "Phase I (002)"),
    diff = simulated - published
  )
stopifnot(nrow(tab_red) == 4L, !anyNA(tab_red$simulated))

tab_red |>
  dplyr::select(population, schedule, published, simulated, typical, diff) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Population" = population,
    "Schedule (1200 mg)" = schedule,
    "Published max reduction (%)" = published,
    "Simulated median max reduction (%)" = simulated,
    "Typical-value max reduction (%)" = typical,
    "Difference (points)" = diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)

# A cohort of 200 per scenario puts the median within about 1-2 points of its
# population value: the four differences were +0.8, -1.8, +1.4 and -0.1 points
# with 200 per scenario and +1.3, -0.9, -0.5 and -0.5 with 500. A mis-transcribed IC50, IC50 study effect or
# IC50 variance moves these by more than 5 points (the typical-value column,
# which drops the IIV, is up to 6 points off in the phase I population).
stopifnot(
  all(abs(tab_red$diff) < 5),
  abs(mean(tab_red$diff)) < 3
)
```

# MO PK model: microdose versus therapeutic doses

## NCA of individual clearance and volume (Figure 3A)

The paper's non-compartmental exploration (Figure 3A) found mean individual
clearance of 63.2 L/h after the microdose versus 14.2 L/h at therapeutic doses,
and mean volume (Dose / lambda_z / AUC0-inf) of 855.0 versus 81.41 L. The
cohorts below are simulated from the MO PK model on the published sampling
schedules: the microdose study sampled to 48 h after a 0.25 h infusion, and the
phase I study at the end of a 0.5 h infusion and 0.25-24 h afterwards
(Supplemental material 1). The therapeutic arm uses 400 mg, inside the
25-1200 mg range of the pooled NCA.

```{r mo-events}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20260618)
n_mo <- 200L
t_micro <- c(0, 0.25, 0.33, 0.42, 0.58, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 18, 24, 36, 48)
t_ther <- c(0, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2.5, 4.5, 7.5, 10.5, 24)

make_pk_arm <- function(ids, dose, dur, times, ext001, treatment, obs_cmt = "central") {
  dosing <- tibble::tibble(
    id = ids, time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = dose, dur = dur, cmt = "central"
  )
  obs <- tidyr::crossing(id = ids, time = times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 0L, amt = NA_real_, dur = NA_real_, cmt = obs_cmt)
  dplyr::bind_rows(dosing, obs) |>
    dplyr::mutate(STUDY_S65487_EXT001 = ext001, treatment = treatment) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

ev_mo <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  make_pk_arm(seq_len(n_mo), 0.1, 0.25, t_micro, 1L, "Microdose 0.1 mg"),
  make_pk_arm(n_mo + seq_len(n_mo), 400, 0.5, t_ther, 0L, "Therapeutic 400 mg")
)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(ev_mo[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))

sim_mo <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_mo, events = ev_mo, keep = c("treatment")) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r mo-pknca}
# Integrator noise at the far tail can undershoot zero by about atol.
stopifnot(all(sim_mo$Cc >= -1e-6 * max(sim_mo$Cc), na.rm = TRUE))
conc_mo <- sim_mo |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Cc = pmax(Cc, 0))
conc_mo <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  conc_mo,
  conc_mo |> dplyr::distinct(id, treatment) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, treatment, time)

dose_mo <- ev_mo |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, dur, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_mo, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
  dose_mo, amt ~ time | treatment + id,
  route = "intravascular", duration = "dur"
)
intervals_mo <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE,
  cl.obs = TRUE, vz.obs = TRUE
)
nca_mo <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals_mo))

# Doses are in mg and Cc in ug/L, so Dose/AUC is in mg/(ug*h/L) = 1000 L/h.
ind_mo <- as.data.frame(nca_mo) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("aucinf.obs", "cl.obs", "vz.obs")) |>
  dplyr::select(id, treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    cl.obs = cl.obs * 1000,
    vz.obs = vz.obs * 1000,
    dn_auc = aucinf.obs / ifelse(grepl("Microdose", treatment), 0.1, 400) / 1000
  )
stopifnot(nrow(ind_mo) == 2L * n_mo)

sim_means <- ind_mo |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    cl.obs = mean(cl.obs, na.rm = TRUE),
    vz.obs = mean(vz.obs, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
published_nca <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~cl.obs, ~vz.obs,
  "Microdose 0.1 mg", 63.2, 855.0,
  "Therapeutic 400 mg", 14.2, 81.41
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = sim_means,
  reference = published_nca,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cl.obs = "L/h", vz.obs = "L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = "Mean individual NCA clearance and volume: MO PK model simulation vs. Burlot 2026 Figure 3A (observed). * differs from reference by >20%."
)
```

```{r fig3a, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
ind_mo |>
  dplyr::select(id, treatment, dn_auc, cl.obs, vz.obs) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(dn_auc, cl.obs, vz.obs)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(name = factor(
    name,
    levels = c("dn_auc", "cl.obs", "vz.obs"),
    labels = c("Dose-normalized AUC (h/L)", "Cl (L/h)", "V (L)")
  )) |>
  ggplot(aes(treatment, value, fill = treatment)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = "Individual value", fill = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3A of Burlot 2026 with simulated subjects from the MO PK model."
  ) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank())
```

The microdose clearance comes out close to the observed mean because, far
below both Km values, the Michaelis-Menten elimination acts as an extra
first-order clearance of VmaxElimination / KmElimination = 892.5 / 17.7 = 50.4
L/h on top of the linear 10.5 L/h. Both volume rows exceed the 20% flag
(about 550 L simulated vs 855 L observed for the microdose, about 100 L vs
81 L at therapeutic doses). The published volumes are Dose / lambda_z / AUC
from five microdose subjects and from the 24 h therapeutic sampling window, so
lambda_z is poorly determined in both, and the paper does not report them as
model-fitting targets. The values are left as published; the model is not
adjusted to match them.

```{r mo-check}
# The ratio of the two clearances is the nonlinearity the MO PK model was
# built to capture (observed ratio of means 63.2 / 14.2 = 4.5). The median
# ratio is used because it is robust to which subjects land in the tails; it
# came out at 5.8 here (ratio of means 5.0), with a cohort-to-cohort spread of
# roughly +/- 0.5. A lost Michaelis-Menten arm or a units slip in Vmax
# collapses the ratio towards 1 or moves it tenfold.
med_cl <- ind_mo |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment) |>
  dplyr::summarise(cl = median(cl.obs, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
ratio_cl <- med_cl$cl[grepl("Microdose", med_cl$treatment)] /
  med_cl$cl[grepl("Therapeutic", med_cl$treatment)]
ratio_cl
stopifnot(ratio_cl > 3, ratio_cl < 8)
```

## Exposure at the microdose: PhI-II versus MO PK model (Figure 4)

Figure 4 shows that the PhI-II PK model over-predicted the microdose AUC
about 4.8-fold (mean pAUC/oAUC) and the MO PK model about 1.1-fold. Both are
ratios to the same observed AUCs, so the typical-value AUC0-48h of the two
models after the 0.1 mg microdose should differ by about 4.8 / 1.1 = 4.4-fold.
The PhI-II model's PK does not depend on the study covariate.

```{r fig4}
t_typ <- seq(0, 48, by = 0.05)
ev_typ_mo <- make_pk_arm(1L, 0.1, 0.25, t_typ, 1L, "Microdose 0.1 mg")
ev_typ_pkpd <- make_pk_arm(1L, 0.1, 0.25, t_typ, 1L, "Microdose 0.1 mg",
                           obs_cmt = "bcl2_bim") |>
  dplyr::mutate(STUDY_S65487_003 = 0L)
auc48 <- function(mod, ev) {
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev, omega = NA, sigma = NA,
                       useLinCmt = FALSE) |>
    as.data.frame()
  stopifnot(nrow(s) == length(t_typ))
  sum(diff(s$time) * (head(s$Cc, -1) + tail(s$Cc, -1)) / 2)
}
auc_pkpd <- auc48(mod_pkpd, ev_typ_pkpd)
auc_mo <- auc48(mod_mo, ev_typ_mo)
tibble::tibble(
  model = c("PhI-II PK/PD model", "MO PK model"),
  `Typical AUC0-48h (ug*h/L)` = c(auc_pkpd, auc_mo)
) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 4)
auc_ratio <- auc_pkpd / auc_mo
auc_ratio
# Deterministic typical-value solves; the published 4.8 and 1.1 are means of
# per-subject ratios in five subjects, so allow +/- 25% around 4.4.
stopifnot(auc_ratio > 3.3, auc_ratio < 5.5)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Infusion durations.** The paper gives no infusion duration. The sampling
  schedules in Supplemental material 1 place the end of infusion at 0.25 h in
  the microdose study and at about 0.5 h in the phase I study (the phase I/II
  study sampled 0.33 h after the start of infusion and again at its end). The
  simulations use 0.25 h for the microdose and 0.5 h for every therapeutic dose,
  including the Figure 2 scenarios.
- **IIV scale.** Tables 2 and 3 give IIV as CV%. Monolix reports log-normal
  random effects as `100 * sqrt(exp(omega^2) - 1)`, so the variances are
  `log(1 + CV^2)`. The alternative reading (CV% = 100 * omega) would give an IC50
  standard deviation of 13.9 on the log scale. The variance reading reproduces
  the paper's population-median maximum reductions (table above).
- **Correlations.** The Cl-Vcentral correlations are printed to one decimal
  (0.6 and 0.5) and are used as printed.
- **IC50 study effect.** Table 2 prints beta-IC50 STUDY003 = -1.6 on log(IC50),
  giving 140.9 * exp(-1.6) = 28.4 ug/L for study 003, while the Results text
  quotes 29.4 ug/L (which corresponds to -1.567, inside the rounding of -1.6).
  The model uses the tabulated -1.6. The text's 140 ug/L for study 002 is the
  rounded Table 2 value 140.9.
- **Residual error form.** The paper says "combined" without naming the Monolix
  variant. The models use `combined1()` (SD = a + b * f), the Monolix default.
- **MO PK microdose proportional error.** Table 3 prints the microdose
  proportional error as 0.1 with unit '%'. The model reads it as a fraction
  (10%), consistent with the unitless 0.5 printed for the therapeutic-dose
  proportional error; 0.1% would be an implausibly small assay error.
- **Residual-error switch.** The MO PK model's two combined error models are
  selected with `STUDY_S65487_EXT001` (1 = microdose study). In the source, the
  study, the dose level, the population and the assay all coincide.
- **Schematic labels.** Supplementary Figure S2 draws the Q2 and Q3 arrows next
  to the opposite peripheral compartments; the caption and Table 2 pair Q2 with
  V2 (1st peripheral) and Q3 with V3 (2nd peripheral), which the model follows.
- **Units.** Doses are in mg and concentrations in ug/L, so `Cc = central / vc
  * 1000`. VmaxElimination and VmaxDistribution are in ug/h and are divided by
  1000 to give mg/h fluxes. R0 is the Bcl2/Bim complex concentration normalized
  by total protein; Table 2 gives its unit as ug/L, which the model carries.
- **Saturable distribution names.** VmaxDistribution and KmDistribution are
  named `vmax_peripheral2` and `km_peripheral2`, following the
  `vmax_<destination>` / `km_<destination>` pattern used for other saturable
  transfers out of the central compartment.
- **Base PK/PD model.** Table 2 also lists a base PK/PD model without the study
  effect and the Cl-Vcentral correlation; only the final PhI-II PK/PD model is
  packaged. The intermediate PhI-II PK model refitted with the microdose data,
  whose estimates are not reported, is not packaged.
- No erratum or correction notice was found for the article as of 2026-11-13.
